Beta, why didn't you visit last Diwali? Dadi missed you all so much. The house felt empty without your laughter.
Dadi: Arre Rohan, you've grown so tall! But look at that shirt, it's all wrinkled. Come, let me iron it for you. Mummy: Thanks Amma, he's been so careless lately.
Papa: Nana ji, the kids are fighting again over toys. They don't listen. Nana: Patience beta, it's all part of growing up in a big family like ours.
Didi: Chacha, remember when we played Holi here as kids? Those were the days. Chacha: Yes, but now everyone is so busy, no time for fun.
Grandma: Oh dear, your cough sounds bad. Have you seen a doctor? Mum: Don't worry, it's just a cold from the trip here.
Rohan: Nani, why is everyone so quiet today? Nani: We're remembering your great-grandpa. He loved these family visits.
Asha: Bhai, Dadi made your favorite gulab jamun! But I burnt my hand helping in the kitchen. Bhai: Ouch, careful didi!
Papa: Chachi, the traffic was terrible coming here. Almost gave up. Chachi: But you're here now, that's what matters. Family first.
Dadi: Look at little Priya, she's shy with all of us. Come to Dadi, beta. Priya: Nooo! Mummy: She's overwhelmed by so many relatives.
Nana: We used to celebrate Rakhi with such joy, all siblings together. Now scattered everywhere. Sigh.
Mum: Dada ji, the kids are excited to see you! They brought drawings. Dada: Wonderful, my little artists!
Chacha: Beta, don't eat so many sweets. You'll get a stomachache like last time. Rohan: But it's Diwali!
Didi: Nani, your stories about old times make me miss Papa's side of the family. Nani: They were always so lively.
Papa: Maasi, why so glum? Maasi: Just tired of everyone forgetting my birthday last month.
Grandpa: Priya, hide and seek with Grandpa? Priya: Yes! But don't tell Mummy I'm late for dinner.
Asha: Dadi, the house is fuller now with everyone here, but I feel out of place sometimes. Dadi: Nonsense, you're family.
Bhai: Chachi, your cooking is the best, but too spicy for the kids! Chachi: Adjust kar lo, beta!
